artifact_metadata.title: Guardian Alpha V30 Stage 2F - Statistical Selection-Bias Recalculation
artifact_metadata.evaluation_sample: Tier 2 Validation (2020-01-02 to 2021-12-31, 505 sessions, 504 return days)

sharpe_estimator_asymptotics.framework: Mertens (2002) / Lo (2002) Non-Normal Sharpe Ratio Asymptotics

deflated_sharpe_ratio_bailey_lopez_de_pr.framework: Bailey & López de Prado (2014) The Deflated Sharpe Ratio
deflated_sharpe_ratio_bailey_lopez_de_pr.formula_expected_max_null: SR* = sigma_SR * ((1 - gamma_euler) * norm_inv(1 - 1/M) + gamma_euler * norm_inv(1 - 1/(M*e)))
deflated_sharpe_ratio_bailey_lopez_de_pr.probability_interpretation: DSR is the cumulative probability that the true strategy Sharpe exceeds the expected maximum Sharpe generated by random chance over M trials. A DSR of 0.5070 means the observed Sharpe is at the 50.7th percentile of the null distribution of maximums (p-value = 0.4930).

multiple_testing_haircut_harvey_liu_zhu.framework: Harvey, Liu, & Zhu (2016) Multiple Testing in Financial Economics
multiple_testing_haircut_harvey_liu_zhu.haircut_mechanism: Empirical t-statistic hurdle rises from 1.96 to 3.00+ as M increases. Adjusted Sharpe = Nominal Sharpe * (t_adjusted / t_unadjusted).
multiple_testing_haircut_harvey_liu_zhu.audit_conclusion: Across all plausible trial dependence specifications, the nominal Tier 2 Sharpe ratio of 1.63 is significantly inflated by sample reuse and multiple testing. The defensible selection-adjusted Sharpe ratio lies in the range of 0.62 to 1.01.
